name: 広島つけ麺 かず 光町本店 (Hiroshima Tsukemen Kazu (Hikarimachi Honten))

claims.text: The dipping dashi for Hiroshima tsukemen is built on chashu and a savory soy-based sauce, which conventionally contains wheat; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The signature broth is made with pork chashu, so the kitchen handles animal products throughout the core dish.
Menu includes breaded/deep-fried oysters (kaki fry) and other fried items shared with wheat-based cooking; no dedicated gluten-free fryer or protocol is documented.
Japanese-style dishes use standard soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.
The kitchen centers on seafood (oysters, anago, octopus, sashimi) and meat; vegetable dishes would share equipment and fish/dashi-based seasonings.
Dishes are seasoned with soy-sauce-based seasonings; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Cooking is centered on a shared hearth, kiln and charcoal grill used for fish, oysters and meat, so vegetable items would share fire and surfaces with animal proteins.

name: 本家 村長の店 (Honke Soncho no Mise)

claims.text: Dishes are cooked on a shared teppan (griddle) where wheat-batter okonomiyaki and noodles are prepared, making cross-contact with gluten effectively unavoidable.
Okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki/Worcestershire-style sauce, which is wheat- and soy-based.
The single shared teppan is used for pork, egg, seafood and cheese dishes, so any item would share the same cooking surface as animal products.
No gluten-free handling is documented; the menu includes fried items (tuna rare-cutlet), and Japanese izakaya cooking relies on wheat-based soy sauce, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
As a traditional Japanese izakaya, standard soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used across sashimi, simmered and grilled dishes; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
Menu is centered on fish, oysters, anago, chicken, horse and beef, with bonito dashi typical of the cuisine; no vegan preparations are documented.

name: 一楽章　未完成 (Ichigakusho Mikansei)

claims.text: The curry is cooked without any oil/fat, using a base of vegetables, fruits, and spices, which can suit health-conscious and lighter-eating diners.

name: 一麺天に通ず (Ichimen Ten ni Tsuzu)

claims.text: The broths are shoyu (soy-sauce) based, and standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat.
Broths are made from fish and shellfish (nodoguro, bonito, shrimp), so no bowl can be made vegan or vegetarian on request.

The signature anago-meshi is finished with a sweet soy-based tare, and Japanese soy sauce is typically brewed with wheat, so the dish should be treated as containing gluten unless the kitchen confirms otherwise.
The house rice is cooked in a dashi made from eel head, bones and kombu, so even the rice is not vegetarian.
